source_read: PMC HTML (PMC6732053, author manuscript; Addiction 2019;114:1738-1750): structured abstract, Introduction, Methods (search, inclusion/exclusion, Table 1 all 25 rows, data extraction, CMR/SMR/RR calculation, analysis), Results (CMR, SMR, RR, meta-regression, sensitivity) with Tables 2-3, Discussion, Limitations, Conclusions, acknowledgements, conflicts, and selected reference entries (17, 18, 36, 44, 45, 48). Figures 1-3 (PRISMA, forest plots) are images; supplementary appendices (.docx) not opened.

claims.overstatement: None material. Two precision points: (1) the cohort description 'mostly people in treatment, people who inject drugs or people with hospital diagnoses' omits the criminal-justice cohorts, including the second-largest (Chen 2010, 21,149 drug offenders in Taiwan; also Ericsson 2014, Forsyth 2018, Karjalainen 2010); (2) 'I2 97-98%' is right for the all-cause CMR (96.9%) and SMR (98.0%) but not for all cause-specific SMRs (homicide 13.6%, cardiovascular 54.9%, drug poisoning 75.3%). The SMR compares users with the whole general population (which includes users), and cause-of-death ascertainment was often unclear; 'drug poisoning' is not specific to amphetamines.
claims.note: All numbers reproduce from Table 2 and Results. But the source reports its headline SMR inconsistently: 6.83 (5.27-8.84) in abstract, Results and Table 2; 6.08 (4.41-8.37; 'n=23') in the sensitivity paragraph; '6.3-fold' and 'around 6.2-fold' in the Discussion. And '8 author-reported + 13 imputed' makes 21 SMRs, not the 23 pooled. The claim's figures (6.83; 5.71 for the 8 author-reported) match the abstract and Table 2.

anchors.locator: Results > Crude mortality rates, 1st paragraph; Table 2 (all-cause row)
anchors.extracted: 23 of 25 cohorts (n=115,223) pooled: all-cause CMR 1.11 per 100 person-years (0.90-1.37), I2 96.9%; regional CMRs from 0.49 (central Europe, 1 study) to 2.02 (Southeast Asia, 2 studies).

All-cause SMR 6.83 (5.27-8.84), 23 studies, I2 98.0%; SMRs computed as cohort CMR divided by GBD 2017 CMR for the respective age, sex, location and years. Men 4.68 (3.43-6.40), women 5.91 (3.74-9.35). No significant regional difference.

Cause-specific SMR: drug poisoning 24.70 (16.67-36.58; 5 studies; I2 75.3%), suicide 12.20 (4.89-30.47; 6; 97.7%), homicide 11.90 (7.82-18.12; 4; 13.6%), cardiovascular 5.12 (3.74-7.00; 4; 54.9%), accidental injury 5.12 (2.88-9.08; 7; 95.5%). Cause-specific CMRs 0.03-0.20 per 100 PY.

anchors.locator: Methods > Calculation of CMR, SMR and RR; Results > Sensitivity analyses
anchors.extracted: SMRs imputed by the reviewers for 13 cohorts (refs 17-30). Author-reported SMRs only (8 cohorts): 5.71 (4.44-7.35), compared in the text with 'our pooled all-cause SMR of 6.08 (4.41-8.37; n=23)'. Excluding the HIV cohort: CMR 1.09 (0.97-1.22), SMR 6.47 (4.96-8.43). Funnel plots and cohort-size analysis reported (Appendix J) as showing no evidence of bias.

Cohorts: treatment, hospital, needle-exchange, injecting-drug-user, criminal-justice, conscript, HIV and school samples; sizes 35-74,170 (abstract 74,139). Cause-of-death ascertainment often unclear; definitions of regular/dependent use varied; polydrug use and comorbidity could not be examined; city-based samples had higher CMRs than national ones (meta-regression p<0.001, adjusted R2 61%).

key_findings.correction: Person-years recomputed from Table 1: 752,292 (includes Weber 2015's implausible 31,215 person-years for 261 people).
Confirmed from Table 3; note the Results text says methodological features were not associated with CMRs or SMRs, which Table 3's case-ascertainment result (p=0.010) contradicts.

reporting_issues.note: Ref 18 = Callaghan et al. 2012, all-cause mortality in methamphetamine-related disorders; ref 36 = Callaghan et al. 2013, motor vehicle accident mortality.
Regional n and study counts sum to 115,223 and 23.

risk_of_bias.note: Low confidence is defensible, but under AMSTAR 2's rating rules 'low' requires one critical flaw; the card scores no critical item 'no', which would mechanically give 'moderate'. The card should state which partial-yes critical item it treats as a flaw (item 9, no confounding domain and a summary quality score, is the natural candidate).

interpretation_gap.note: Minor overall; the most consequential element is the Discussion's statement that several causes of death 'appear to be causally related to use', which an SMR against the general population cannot show.

missed: Results: '8 author-reported plus 13 imputed' SMRs make 21, not the 23 said to be pooled; the imputed set is cited as references 17-30, which spans 14 references.

Results > Factors associated with CMR and SMR says methodological features were not associated with CMRs or SMRs, but Table 3 shows case ascertainment associated with the CMR (coefficient 0.748, SE 0.076, p=0.010, adjusted R2 34.9%).
Table 1: Weber 2015 lists 261 participants with 31,215 person-years of follow-up (about 120 years each), implausible for the amphetamine subgroup and inflating the review's total person-years.

For cl_meth_mortality: the claim's cohort description omits criminal-justice cohorts (Chen 2010, 21,149 people; Ericsson 2014; Forsyth 2018; Karjalainen 2010), and its 'I2 97-98%' applies to the all-cause estimates only (cause-specific SMR I2 ranges 13.6% to 97.7%).
